questions.stem: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has capped trade margins on anti-cancer medicines, prompting scrutiny of how drug prices are regulated in India. With reference to NPPA, which one of the following best describes its institutional status?
options: It is an executive body set up by a government resolution, exercising price-control powers delegated under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order
It is a statutory body created directly under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 with independent rule-making powers over drug prices
It is a constitutional authority established under Article 323B to adjudicate pharmaceutical pricing disputes
It is a statutory regulator under the Ministry of Health, functioning similarly to the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation
questions.explanation: NPPA was constituted in 1997 by a government resolution as an attached office under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, not by an Act of Parliament, so it is not statutory in itself. It exercises price-fixation powers through the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, which is issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. There is no Article 323B tribunal for drug pricing, and NPPA sits under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, not Health.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Financial protection for patients cannot be achieved through a single intervention: former National Health Authority CEO
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory vs executive/non-statutory distinction among regulatory bodies; similar to UPSC questions distinguishing constitutional, statutory and executive bodies (e.g., NHRC vs CIC vs NITI Aayog).

questions.stem: The Finance Ministry's October review credits recent GST Council reforms with easing compliance for businesses. Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The GST Council is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution.
The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council.
The Supreme Court, in the Mohit Minerals case (2022), held that recommendations of the GST Council are not binding on the Union and the States.
GST Council recommendations require a majority of not less than three-fourths of weighted votes cast, with the Centre having one-third weightage.
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct. Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment) created the GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister; in Mohit Minerals v. Union of India (2022), the Supreme Court held Council recommendations are only recommendatory, not binding; and Article 279A(9) prescribes the three-fourths weighted-majority voting formula with the Centre's one-third weightage.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Economy can sustain high-growth trajectory in FY27, recent GST reforms to help: Finmin review
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A composition/voting and the Mohit Minerals ruling on cooperative federalism; similar to past prelims questions on GST Council powers and composition.

Coal India Limited has been conferred "Navratna" status, one rung below the highest "Maharatna" category of Central Public Sector Enterprises.
The Government of India continues to hold a majority stake of more than 50 percent in Coal India Limited.
questions.explanation: Coal India functions under the Ministry of Coal, and the Government holds a majority (around 63%) shareholding, making statements 1 and 3 correct. Statement 2 is wrong because Coal India holds "Maharatna" status — the highest CPSE category — not the lower "Navratna" tier.

questions.stem: A cartoon on bauxite mining in the Eastern Ghats draws attention to the legal safeguards governing mineral extraction in tribal hill tracts. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The bauxite-rich hill tracts of the Eastern Ghats fall largely within Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas.
The Samatha judgment (1997) held that government land in Scheduled Areas can be freely leased to non-tribal private mining companies.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 mandates that Gram Sabhas be consulted before land acquisition for development projects in Scheduled Areas.
In the Niyamgiri case, the Supreme Court allowed the state government alone to decide on diversion of forest land for bauxite mining, without requiring Gram Sabha consent.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the bauxite tracts of the Eastern Ghats (Visakhapatnam Agency, Koraput-Rayagada belt) lie in Fifth Schedule areas, and PESA mandates Gram Sabha consultation before land acquisition there. Statement 2 is wrong — the Samatha judgment held the opposite, barring leasing of such land to non-tribal private companies. Statement 4 is wrong — in the Niyamgiri case the Supreme Court required the matter to be decided by the Gram Sabhas, not the state government alone.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: On bauxite mining in the Eastern Ghats | Green Humour by Rohan Chakravarty
questions.pyqLink: Tests Fifth Schedule protections, the Samatha judgment and PESA's Gram Sabha consent mechanism; similar to past prelims questions on Fifth Schedule and tribal land rights.

questions.stem: India's Patent Office rejected a patent application for the BPaL regimen used in drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The BPaL regimen combines bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, and is recommended by the WHO for certain forms of drug-resistant tuberculosis.
Under the Indian Patents Act, 1970, pharmaceutical process patents are prohibited entirely, and only product patents may be granted for drugs.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — BPaL is a six-month all-oral WHO-recommended regimen for eligible drug-resistant TB patients. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Patents Act, 1970 allows both process and product patents (product patents for drugs were introduced only after the 2005 TRIPS-compliant amendment); it does not prohibit process patents.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements in the context of global economic conditions in October 2026:
statements: Statement-I: International agencies including the IMF and World Bank revised India's growth forecast upward to 7% or above.
Statement-II: The US Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates elevated strengthens the dollar and tends to trigger capital outflow pressure on emerging market economies.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are independently correct: global agencies upgraded India's growth outlook on the strength of domestic consumption, investment and GST-related reforms, while the Fed's elevated-rate stance separately makes US assets more attractive, pressuring emerging-market currencies and capital flows. The Fed's decision does not explain India's upward growth revision — if anything it works against it — so Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the revision of electoral rolls in India. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The preparation and revision of electoral rolls is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Form 7 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 is used to object to the inclusion of a name or to seek deletion of an entry from the electoral roll.
The Election Commission of India is empowered under Article 324 of the Constitution to superintend, direct and control the preparation of electoral rolls.
An objection seeking deletion of a voter's name through Form 7 can only be filed by the elector whose own name is sought to be deleted, and by no one else.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct static facts on electoral roll law. Statement 4 is false — as the Delhi SIR case shows, Form 7 objections against a voter's entry can be filed by any other elector or booth-level agent, not only by the voter concerned, which is precisely what triggers disenfranchisement concerns.

questions.stem: With reference to tropical cyclones affecting India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean basin form mainly during the pre-monsoon (April-May) and post-monsoon (October-December) periods.
Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal are generally more frequent and intense than those in the Arabian Sea, mainly due to higher sea surface temperatures and lower vertical wind shear.
Names for cyclones forming in the North Indian Ocean are assigned by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) alone, without reference to any regional international body.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are established climatological facts about North Indian Ocean cyclone seasonality and the Bay of Bengal's higher intensity. Statement 3 is false — names are drawn from a rotational list contributed by 13 member countries of the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones; IMD, as the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre, issues the name but does not decide alone.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements on India's institutional framework for cyclone disaster management. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has the Prime Minister as its ex-officio chairperson.
The Disaster Management Act, 2005 provides for a State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) in every state, headed by the Chief Minister.
The National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with World Bank assistance.
India's zero-casualty approach to cyclone management relies solely on permanent concrete cyclone shelters, without any need for evacuation.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe the NDMA and SDMA structure under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. Statement 3 is false — NCRMP is implemented by NDMA/state governments under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Environment Ministry. Statement 4 is false — the mass pre-emptive evacuation of over 55,000 people and 3,100 pregnant women ahead of Cyclone Arnab shows evacuation, not shelters alone, is central to the zero-casualty strategy.

questions.sourceTitle: Cyclone Arnab LIVE: Cyclone wreaks havoc in Odisha, over 55,000 evacuated across 9 districts

questions.stem: With reference to autoimmune diseases, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system produces antibodies that attack the body's own healthy tissues, including skin, joints and kidneys.
All autoimmune diseases are caused solely by single-gene mutations inherited in a strict Mendelian pattern, similar to sickle cell anemia.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly describes lupus as an autoimmune disease where self-antibodies attack the body's own tissues, consistent with the ICMR-funded study on multiplex SLE families. Statement 2 is false — autoimmune diseases are generally polygenic and multifactorial, shaped by both genetic predisposition and environmental triggers, unlike monogenic Mendelian disorders such as sickle cell anemia.

The United Nations agency responsible for declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern

Pair 4 is incorrect — a PHEIC is declared by the WHO Director-General under the IHR, not by UNICEF, which has no such mandate.

questions.stem: With reference to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR), which one of the following best describes the procedure?
options: It is an open-heart surgical procedure in which the chest is surgically opened to replace a diseased aortic valve under cardiopulmonary bypass.
It is a minimally invasive, catheter-based procedure used to implant a new valve inside a diseased native aortic valve without the need for open-heart surgery.
It is a pacemaker implantation technique used to correct abnormal heart rhythms arising from valve defects.
It is a diagnostic imaging procedure used to visualise blockages in the coronary arteries prior to valve surgery.
questions.explanation: TAVR, as used in the Kauvery Hospital case, is precisely the minimally invasive catheter-based valve replacement technique described in option B, avoiding open-heart surgery. Option A describes the traditional open surgical alternative TAVR is designed to replace; C confuses it with pacemaker implantation; D confuses it with coronary angiography, a diagnostic rather than therapeutic procedure.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements regarding the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
statements: Statement-I: Despite the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo crossing 10,000 confirmed cases, researchers currently consider a major outbreak in most other countries unlikely.
Statement-II: Ebola virus disease spreads mainly through airborne transmission, which makes sustained international spread highly likely once a single case crosses a border.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct and matches the article, where researchers judge most other countries unlikely to face significant spread currently. Statement-II is factually incorrect — Ebola virus disease spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected persons or animals, not through airborne transmission, which is a key distinguishing static fact about the disease.

questions.sourceTitle: Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
questions.pyqLink: Tests mode of transmission of Ebola versus airborne diseases, a recurring static Science distinction UPSC uses to test precision over assumption.

questions.stem: With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Election Commission derives its power to prepare and revise electoral rolls from Article 324 of the Constitution read with the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
The final electoral rolls prepared after a Special Intensive Revision require prior ratification by the concerned State Legislative Assembly before they can be published.
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and elections in the Election Commission, and the Representation of the People Act, 1950 governs preparation of rolls, making statement 1 correct. Statement 2 is false — the Commission publishes final rolls on its own authority through the State CEOs; no legislative ratification is required, as seen in the EC extending SIR deadlines in Delhi, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana and Nagaland on its own order.

statements: Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is a public sector undertaking jointly owned by the Government of Telangana and the Government of India.
Coal mining in India was brought under government control through the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, with non-coking coal mines nationalised in 1973.
Under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, the regulation of minor minerals is vested exclusively in the Central Government.
questions.explanation: SCCL is indeed a joint-sector company with majority equity held by the Telangana government and the rest by the Union government, matching its mining operations described in the Telangana article. Coking coal mines were nationalised in 1972 and non-coking coal mines in 1973 under the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, making statement 2 correct. Statement 3 is false — under the MMDR Act, 1957, State Governments (not the Centre) are empowered to make rules for regulating minor minerals.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the cheetah and its reintroduction in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Kuno National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh, is the reintroduction site for cheetahs brought from Namibia and South Africa under Project Cheetah.
The cheetah is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which accords it the highest level of legal protection in India.
The African cheetah, native to India, became extinct from the Indian subcontinent in the mid-twentieth century.
Cheetahs reintroduced in India are formally classified as 'Critically Endangered' under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh hosts the translocated African cheetahs, and the species is a Schedule I animal under the 1972 Act. Statement 3 is wrong because it was the Asiatic cheetah, not the African cheetah, that was native to India and declared extinct around 1952. Statement 4 is wrong because the Wildlife (Protection) Act uses Schedules, not IUCN categories like 'Critically Endangered', to classify species.

questions.stem: With reference to the India-China boundary, which one of the following best describes the 'McMahon Line'?
options: It is the boundary in the eastern sector agreed upon in 1914 between British India and Tibet at the Simla Convention, which China does not recognise.
It is the ceasefire line established after the 1962 India-China war and mutually accepted by both countries as the Line of Actual Control.
It is the boundary in the western sector demarcated by British surveyors through the Johnson Line proposed in 1865.
It is a boundary settled bilaterally between India and China in 2005 under the Special Representatives' talks on border resolution.
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 at the Simla Convention between British India and Tibet, forming the de facto boundary in the eastern sector including Arunachal Pradesh; China rejects it on the ground that Tibet lacked authority to conclude such an agreement. Option B wrongly conflates it with the Line of Actual Control, which is not a mutually agreed or demarcated line. Option C describes the Johnson Line relevant to the western sector (Aksai Chin), and option D is a fabricated claim — no such 2005 bilateral settlement exists.

questions.sourceTitle: Transgressions keep happening, border normal now: Arunachal CM Pema Khandu
questions.pyqLink: Tests the historical origin of the McMahon Line versus the Johnson Line and the Line of Actual Control — a classic static-current fusion question.
